To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CCND1 and EMYS amplification is frequent in breast cancer, and CCND1 amplifications are associated with poor prognosis in tamoxifen‐ treated breast cancer.
CCND1 and/or EMSY gene amplifications are present in about 20% of breast cancers, and are associated with poor prognosis in patients treated with tamoxifen.
CCND1 and CCND2 amplification is associated in breast cancer and that CCND1 amplifications in tamoxifen treated breast cancer patients is associated with reduced overall survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and more effective treatments for breast cancer.
the development of a new generation of materials for the treatment of breast cancer.
the genetic alterations of the CCND1 and the EMSY genes in breast cancer, and with their possible prognostic and predictive value.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no significant differences in survival between the CCND1 amplified and non‐amplified groups of patients.
the evidence is not yet sufficient to support a recommendation for routine testing for EMSY in clinical practice.
CCND1 and/or EMSY amplification is not a significant prognostic factor in breast cancer patients treated with tamoxifen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CCND1 and CCND2 genes are not the main target of the 11q13 amplicon, but that EMSY is a target gene and that CCND1 amplifications may be associated with poor survival in tamoxifen‐ treated breast cancers.
EMSY is a potential target gene for CCND1 amplifications.
CCND1 amplifications are associated with poor prognosis in ER positive tamoxifen treated patients, and that CCND1 and/or EMSY amplification are not associated with BRCA2 mutation status.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CCND1 amplifications are associated with reduced survival among tamoxifen‐resistant breast cancers, suggesting that CCND1 is a potential target for therapeutic intervention.
the CCND1/EMSY locus is frequently amplified in breast cancers, and that CCND1 and/or EMSY copy number is an independent predictor of poor outcome in tamoxifen‐responsive breast cancers.
EMSY is an important target of 11q13 amplification in breast cancer and may play a role in tamoxifen resistance.
